module_title: The Gender Gap, Child Sex Ratio, and Union Territory Extremes
introduction: At this level, we will analyze the massive disparity between male and female literacy (the Gender Gap), understand the highly alarming 'Child Sex Ratio', and focus on the heavily skewed demographic data of India's Union Territories (UTs).

core_concepts.title: Gender Gap in Literacy
core_concepts.description: While India's overall literacy is 74.04%, there is a massive inequality. The Male Literacy Rate is '82.14%', whereas the Female Literacy Rate is only '65.46%' (a gap of about 16.6%). Surprisingly, 'Rajasthan' is the state with the lowest female literacy rate in India (only 52.1%) and the highest male-female literacy gap.

core_concepts.title: Child Sex Ratio (CSR - 0 to 6 years)
core_concepts.description: This is the number of girls per 1000 boys strictly in the age group of 0 to 6 years. It is a far more alarming metric than the overall sex ratio because India's CSR is only '919' (a decline from 927 in 2001). 'Arunachal Pradesh' (972) has the highest CSR among states, while 'Haryana' (834) has the absolute lowest.

core_concepts.title: UTs: Literacy and Sex Ratio
core_concepts.description: Among Union Territories, 'Lakshadweep' tops in literacy (91.8%). For Sex Ratio, 'Puducherry' (1037) has the highest among UTs, while 'Daman & Diu' has the lowest sex ratio in all of India (an astonishingly low 618 females per 1000 males).

core_concepts.title: Urbanization: Absolute vs. Percentage
core_concepts.description: As learned, 'Goa' is the most urbanized state by *Percentage*. However, if an exam asks for the highest *Absolute* urban population (Total Number of People in cities), the answer is 'Maharashtra' (over 5 crore urban residents), followed closely by Uttar Pradesh.

important_entities.name: Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao
important_entities.significance: It is no geographical coincidence that the Government of India launched this flagship scheme in 2015 from 'Panipat, Haryana'. The primary catalyst was the 2011 Census data, which exposed Haryana as having both the worst overall sex ratio (879) and the worst child sex ratio (834) in the country.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often wonder why Daman & Diu (618) has such a low sex ratio. Is female feticide rampant there? No. The geographical/economic reality is that Daman is a heavy industrial zone that attracts massive 'male-only migrant labor' from across the country. This male-dominated influx artificially skews the ratio.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In multiple-choice questions, do not select 0-5 or 0-7. The Child Sex Ratio is calculated exclusively for the 0-6 years demographic.

exam_strategy_tips: A very common trap: The state with the lowest *Female* Literacy is NOT Bihar; it is 'Rajasthan' (52.1%). Remember this exception.
Never mix up the Child Sex Ratio (919) data with the Overall Sex Ratio (943) data. Examiners frequently swap them in Assertion-Reasoning questions.
